text:
Lukas Dostal came into this season with a track record that argued for patience, and he is testing it. Through 14 games he has an .857 save percentage and a 4-7-1 record, and he has allowed 6.8 goals more than an average goalie would on the shots he faced (47 on 40.2 expected), 13th percentile. Last season was close to neutral by our numbers (-3.7 in 56 games), and Evolving-Hockey's own scale liked his last two seasons a good deal more.

What hurts is the mix. He's at .929 on low-danger shots against a league .962, the goals teams can't live with, and .638 on high-danger ones against .684. The recent run hasn't turned it: he was out after 20 minutes at Calgary on Nov. 6, gave up six to the Islanders on Nov. 14, and CBS Sports' line on Monday's loss in Seattle was "Beaten three times in third period." Our talent range still puts his true level near league average, which is the case for staying patient. You'd want to see the easy saves come back first; those are the ones that turn a losing record around.
headline: Lukas Dostal is testing Anaheim's patience
